newsitem.title: UK: Ldn Freight - Grains lead Atlantic Panamax demand.
newsitem.headline: Ldn Freight - Grains lead Atlantic Panamax demand.

text.p: Stronger demand for Panamaxes in the freight market was led by grain charterers in the Atlantic and minerals charterers in the Pacific.

Modern vessels continued to attract a widening premium over older types, especially from Far Eastern charterers. The BFI jumped 19 points to 1406 on the strength of hardening Panamax rates. Some brokers saw the current situation as ominous for charterers since the current build-up is occurring even before the Chinese New Year holidays are complete. The Caper scene remained largely featureless but some owners' brokers said conditions for modern Handies were showing a few signs of improvement in the Atlantic.

E Coast S America has become increasingly active. Angelic Faith 65,000 dwt was fixed delivery Brazil Feb 15/28 for 4-6 months Atlantic trading at $10,500 daily plus $250,000 bonus, possibly by Shipmair. Lalemant were linked with ROR 35,662 dwt on subjects for Brazil/Continent business, although others believed these charterers had fixed a Panamax as well.

Theonymphos 66,713 dwt was rumoured fixed from the Plate or Brazil to the Continent at over $17,000 daily, and Tradigrain booked a Panamax for 50,000 wheat Bahia Blanca/India on private terms. Glencore quoted fresh orders of 50,000/5 heavy grain Up River and Bahia Blanca/China for end Feb and 50,000 heavy grain to Lisbon/Hamburg for feb/march. Elsewhere mactrar fixed Glencore for 60,000 barley from Rouen and La Pallice to Jeddah at $19.00 basis 2-1 but failed on subjects, and Sometra booked a 27,000 dwt vessel from the Continent to W Africa in the low $6,000s daily. Iranian charterers fixed Astor 64,838 dwt for Australian wheat to Iran at about $16.00.

Linda Oldendorff 75,100 dwt was rumoured fixed by Docenave for 2 or 3 laden legs Atlantic business at $11,250 daily, and Ioannis M 61,451 dwt was believed fixed delivery key wt mid Feb for short period on private terms. Cobelfret were said to have taken a late 1970s built 62,000 dwt vessel for a transatlantic round to cover Norfolk/La Spezia coal at about $8,000 daily. In the East some solid rates were paid for modern Panamaxes for rounds but Oinoussian Navigator 64,556 dwt fixed delivery Taichung mid Feb trip via Australia to Japan by NYK at $11,000 daily and the 1978-built Timios Stavros 64,730 dwt fixed by Halla delivery prompt China for a NoPac round at $9,0 daily were both said to have failed on subjects. Sapphire 68,600 dwt was reported fixed by Klaveness delivery Far East mid Feb for 4-6 or 7-9 months at a firm $11,750 daily.

A better underlying tone for modern Handies in the Atlantic was claimed by some brokers, although conditions remained weak for older types. Alcinoe 34,000 dwt was believed fixed by Star delivery prompt Continent for a trip to New Zealand with fertilizers at about $10,000/10,250 daily. Canadian Rest fixed Elikon 28,234 dwt delivery Continent Feb for about 6 months Lakes trading in the high $7,000's daily, and the craned Friendship-type Agamemnon 23,000 dwt was linked with Kent Line for 12 months timecharter at $7,500 daily. A 45,000 dwt Chinese-controlled craned bulker was believed fixed by Pan Ocean delivery Muscat trip via the Black Sea to the Far East in the high $8,000s daily.
